messages.subject: generating posterior predictive distributions
parts:
In the BDA 3rd edition book there are examples of posterior predictive model checks for the school data, also in Appendix C. But these are done in R, not within Stan. I want to be able to generate the distribution of the maximum values from predicted data within Stan. I saw in a post from 2012 that this was not possible to do (or maybe I misunderstood this).   Is it possible to do now? Is there an example available that generates future data?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] generating posterior predictive distributions
parts:
If you have a set of parameters or generated quantities,
you can declare a generated quantity and define it as
the max of the set. Then you'll get the posterior.

For instance, if you want the max normal from a set of
K normals (i.e., an order statistic), use:

parameters {
real y;
}
model {
y ~ normal(0,1);
}
generated quantities {
real y_max;
y_max <- max(y);
}

You can get all the ranks using sorting.

- Bob

I'll add a simple example in the next edition of the manual.

We added a generated quantities block that makes it easier
to do posterior predictive checks efficiently that independently
sample the posterior predictive quantities from each sample.
They're effectively "cut" from the model.

We discuss this in the manual, but the only example is a
complex one for Gaussian processes in section 16.4.

(Without more context, I won't be able tof ind the old post you're
referring to.)

- Bob
